---
title: "021 — Sync docs with the implementation"
---

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Bring the published documentation back in sync with the product it describes,
by treating factual accuracy as a contract rather than an aspiration: every checkable
claim a page makes is a promise between the page and the product, and the promise is
verified by performing the documented steps against a running stack and by citing code
for every fact — not by re-reading the prose. The Diátaxis restructure (019) had given
the docs a sound shape, but the audit behind this feature found five recurring drift
themes underneath it: the provider how-to still described a seven-template picker when
the registry ships eighteen; the labs guide still told a pre-Postgres story in which
labs lived in a local SQLite database and "no server was involved"; interface labels had
renamed themselves in the UI without the docs following ("Branch from here", "Generate
Lab", a "DB ready (pg)" badge); the two contributor documents contradicted each other on
branch naming and commit convention; and the architecture explanation had fallen behind
the schema, the route map, and the provider layer.

**Why.** The owner's priority ranking settled both the order and the voice of the work:
non-developer readers come first, and within that, the path of least resistance wins.
Beginner tutorials and everyday how-to guides outranked contributor-facing material, and
the docs landing page had to lead with the one-line installer rather than the
development stack — a reader who wants to try Mayon should never wade past pnpm
commands to get started. It also meant complete, plain professional prose throughout:
these pages are written for people using the product, not for people who already know
it, so every fix was an ordinary rewrite rather than a patch of clipped fragments.

**Outcome & reversals.** Landed 2026-09-06, docs-only by construction — no product code
changed. The walkthroughs corrected all five themes: the provider guide now documents
the eighteen-template registry (including GitHub Copilot's server-side sign-in and the
Ollama base URL's `/api` suffix) and denies the "default template" the old page
invented; the labs guide now states plainly that labs persist in the server's Postgres
database, resolving its contradiction with the data-and-privacy guide; the branching
tutorial describes the flat Parents/Branches/Siblings rail, the dedicated /tree page,
and the exact "Branch from this" / "Branch from this text" labels; both contributor
documents now state the convention the repository's own history actually follows
(Conventional Commits, `feat/…`-style prefixes — measured, not assumed, from
`git log` and every local and remote branch); and the architecture page gained the new
routes, the new schema columns and tables, the five provider kinds behind the eighteen
templates, and the product capabilities it had never mentioned. Verification ran at two
levels: every page's steps were performed against a running dev stack, and the claims
were pinned to code (`registry.ts`, `ProviderConfig.svelte`, `ChatRail.svelte`,
`schema.ts`, and the rest) so the next drift has a breadcrumb to follow. The final
consistency pass against the accuracy contract found one residual ambiguity — the
architecture page still said cross-links "render as distinct reference edges", the very
phrasing the walkthrough had struck from the tutorial — and tightened it to name the
Cross-links panel as the only render site. `quarto render docs` stayed at zero
warnings, and the repository gates (`pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`) passed
unchanged. No reversals; the ledger closed with every discrepancy terminal.

**A defect, not a doc fix.** The audit surfaced one product defect, which the docs were
*not* edited to paper over: the server's login rate limiter does not follow the
forwarded-client header the way its own test asserts. With `trustProxy: 1`
(`server/src/server.ts:123-125`), a login from a different `x-forwarded-for` address on
the same socket is expected to be rejected with a 401, but receives a 429 — the
limiter's key (`server/src/auth/index.ts:314`) reads `request.ip`, which does not track
the forwarded header in that position. The failure is deterministic and pre-existing
(285 of 286 server tests pass around it). It is recorded here as the pending fix for a
future feature, per the rule that a product defect is never resolved by bending the
documentation to match broken behavior.

**Learnings.**

- Docs drift is structural, not careless: every theme traced to a feature that shipped
  without its docs in the same change. The fix that lasts is making "update the page in
  the same change" the recorded norm — the decision history already says so; the
  accuracy contract gives it teeth.
- "Perform the steps" and "cite the code" catch different classes of error. Walking the
  UI found wrong labels and missing flows; pinning claims to `file:line` found wrong
  URLs, wrong counts, and the defect above. Docs verification needs both.
- A discrepancy ledger with terminal states (`doc-fixed`, `defect-recorded`,
  `wontfix` + justification) keeps an audit from ending in a shrug: every known
  disagreement ends in exactly one of three named places, none of which is "open".
- The primary-source rule (when two pages overlap, one wins and the others point at it)
  is what turns a docs sync from a whack-a-mole into a consistent corpus.
